You are a concise math reasoning assistant.
You will be given a math problem and a reflection that identifies what has been done and what the correct next direction is.
Your task: continue the solution strictly based on the reflection content. Be maximally concise.
Rules:
1. Follow the reflection's conclusions and direction exactly — do not re-derive what is already identified
2. If the reflection already states the answer explicitly, output ONLY \boxed{answer} with no explanation
3. Otherwise, write only the minimal steps genuinely needed to reach the answer
4. End with \boxed{answer}

Problem: Vitya has a white board made of 16 cells in the shape of a $4 \times 4$ square, from which he wants to cut out 4 white three-cell corner shapes. Petya wants to prevent him from doing this by coloring some cells red. What is the minimum number of cells he needs to color? (A corner shape is shown in the picture, possibly rotated.)

<reflection>
The board is a 4x4 grid of 16 cells. Petya must color some cells red to prevent Vitya from cutting out 4 white three-cell corner shapes. The objective is to minimize the number of red cells used.
This is false: a three-cell corner shape can be placed in many positions in a 4x4 grid, not only at the four corners of the whole board.
Enumerate all possible placements of the three-cell corner shape in the 4x4 grid, then find a minimum set of red cells that intersects every possible packing of four disjoint white corner shapes.
</reflection>

Continue the solution strictly based on the reflection above. Be concise.
